references.text: Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon are mentioned as the place where the Israelites camped, the same place where the Egyptians overtook them.
Pharaoh prepared his chariot and took his army with him, including six hundred chosen chariots, which here pursue the Israelites.
The Egyptians pursued the Israelites into the sea with all Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen.
Moses' song describes Pharaoh's chariots and army that were cast into the sea, a reference to the same military force.
Moses reminds the people how the Lord let the water from the Sea of Reeds flood over the Egyptian army as they pursued them.
Joshua reminds the people that the Egyptians pursued their fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Sea of Reeds.
Nehemiah mentions that God saw the pursuers at the sea, a direct reference to the Egyptian pursuit.
The psalm describes how the sea overwhelmed the enemies who were pursuing the Israelites.
The psalm tells that the water covered over the opponents; none of them remained.
Hebrews mentions that the Egyptians drowned when they tried to cross the Red Sea in pursuit of the Israelites.
Connects the pursuit at the sea (14:9) directly to its divine judgment in the sea (15:19).
Establishes the geographical context for the pursuit by showing the travel route to the same campsite.
Shows the direct consequence of the pursuit: the army that overtook them is destroyed.
Shows how the prophecy about pursuit (14:17) was fulfilled in the event (14:9).
